title: Dispositions -- the states a record may be found in, and what each one means
description: The grammar of reading a record, held once for every kind of record this kit keeps: a run's own receipt, and a judgement of a case against a rubric. A disposition NAMES a shape a record can have and says what it tells a reader. It is a sensor and never a broom: it names a run whose record says something is wrong and stops, because deleting a record of a run is a decision with an author and no machine may be that author. Every disposition carries its own calibration -- one receipt it MUST match and one lookalike it MUST tolerate -- so the sensor proves what it sees before anything is believed on its word. A disposition matches by EQUALITY over the fields it names and nothing else: a comparison language would be behaviour inside a declaration, and the moment a declaration can compute, nothing may generate it.

when.description: The fields this disposition reads and the values it reads them as. A field the reading does not carry reads as null, so a declared null is how a disposition names an ABSENCE -- which is the state that matters most here, since a run that died states nothing at all. What a disposition reads is the receipt as it was FOUND, plus the fields declared below, which no receipt carries and only the reader can know.

in_flight.description: True when the run that opened this record is the very run now reading it. A run cannot judge its own liveness: its record is legitimately unclosed because it has not finished, and a sensor unable to tell that from a corpse would report every healthy run as one. Stated as a READ FIELD rather than as an exemption inside the machine, so that the exclusion is visible, declared, and a host's to tighten.

proves.description: A receipt this disposition MUST match: its evidence that it can see the thing it claims to catch, carried in the declaration rather than in somebody's memory of a test.

admits.description: A lookalike receipt it MUST NOT match. A disposition that cannot state what it tolerates has no measured edge, and a rule with no edge eventually names everything.
